title: Metric-first holdback orchestrator for Hosted/Dedicated/Private rollouts
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: We need a unified, telemetry-driven mechanism that guarantees safe exposure of new model versions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments. Current rollout primitives are environment-specific and lack a shared metric contract and holdback semantics for A/B, canary, and shadow traffic. This ticket implements a Metric-First Holdback Orchestrator: a lightweight controller that enforces metric contracts, computes holdback scoring, triggers staged traffic increases, and executes automated rollback or conversion to shadow mode when thresholds are breached.

Goals:
- Define a minimal metric contract (latency P95, request error rate, end-to-end quality delta via eval hooks) that is enforced across environments.
- Provide holdback strategies (percentage-based canaries, deterministic A/B holdbacks, and shadow-scoring-only deployments) that respect environment constraints (no egress in Private, fixed GPU pools in Dedicated).
- Wire automatic rollback with graduated actions (throttle → isolate → shadow-only → rollback) and a human-notification checkpoint for P0 regressions.
- Keep rollout configs declarative and translatable between Hosted/Dedicated/Private while surfacing environment-specific knobs (e.g., burst capacity window for Dedicated, network tunnel health for Private).
acceptance_criteria: A single metric contract document exists and is stored in the repo (latency P50/P95, error rate, quality delta) with example thresholds for low/medium/high risk.

Holdback controller can start a canary at 5% traffic, ramp to 25% then 50% using time or metric gates in Hosted, and apply equivalent percentage routing semantics in Dedicated by mapping to instance slots.

When quality delta > configured threshold or error rate spike > configured threshold, orchestrator executes graduated response: throttle traffic, convert remaining traffic to shadow, or activate rollback; all actions are logged and emit events to the Console.

Private deployments can opt out of external metrics ingestion; controller falls back to local telemetry adapter and enforces same contract without network egress, with fallback notifications to local on-call and audit log recorded.
Implementation includes unit tests for gating logic and an integration test that simulates a latency spike and verifies automatic conversion to shadow mode and rollback path execution.
A demo runbook and a Console dashboard tab showing holdback state, metric time series, and recent automated actions is available for the SRE and product teams.
tasks: Design metric contract and thresholds with PM and Applied ML (doc + examples)
Implement holdback controller core: metric gate evaluator, staged-ramp engine, and action executor
Add adapters: Hosted router adapter, Dedicated instance-slot mapper, Private local-telemetry adapter
Hook into Console events stream and emit audit-safe actions (including who/why triggered)
End-to-end integration tests using synthetic traffic and failure injection
Create runbook and dashboard surfaces in Console
Security review and KMS audit for Private telemetry export opt-in
notes: Design trade-off: keep metric contract deliberately small to reduce cross-team alignment friction. Start with latency P95, request error rate (5xx/timeout), and an application-level quality delta (from nightly evals or online reranking score).

Dedicated constraint: cannot always increase fractional traffic smoothly. Mapping: percentage -> number of serving slots or routed tenant partitions. Need a stable mapping algorithm to avoid flapping during autoscaling events.

Private constraint: customer networks may block metric export. Implement local adapter that writes events to the local audit log and sends signals via the private control plane channel. Maintain parity by running the same gating logic against local telemetry sources.

Fallback staircase: first throttle (reduce concurrency/requests), then switch remainder to shadow scoring-only, then complete rollback. This sequence avoids hard rollbacks for transient noise and preserves user traffic when possible.

We will reuse the existing rollout orchestration APIs where possible (see ENG-4027 and ENG-7741) but introduce a thin compatibility layer so the controller can express its holdback intent across modes.
Telemetry cost: evaluate cardinality impact of quality delta metrics. If too high, sample requests for quality scoring and extrapolate with confidence intervals.
